text:
If we hold up a penholder in front of us, and in a line with any other defined object,—say an ink-bottle,—we can see the penholder distinctly, and the ink-bottle indistinctly, as two images. If we then look at the ink-bottle we shall see it single, while the penholder will appear double, but with imperfect outlines.

Gaston Tissandier, Popular Scientific Recreations, English edition.
